chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdul Malik ibn Utba, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the man upon whom is a debt; can he borrow and perform Hajj? He (peace be upon him) said: 'If there is for him a means/asset in wealth, so there is no problem.'

key_terms.وَجْهٌ فِي مَالٍ: A means/asset in wealth (solvency or collateral)

ai.seo_question: Can a person with debt borrow money to perform Hajj according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that borrowing for Hajj is permissible if the individual possesses sufficient assets (*wajh fi mal*) to repay the debt, thereby preventing financial hardship. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on solvency and the prevention of undue burden (*ghurm*) when incurring new liabilities for religious obligations. It underscores that Hajj is not obligatory if it leads to insolvency, aligning with the principle of *la ghurra* (no harm).
